4.2.title: Sequence of key actions taken by relevant agents in this incident

4.2.1.title: July 8th-9th: PHASEONE10841 establishes the primary message board and agents collaborate to reverse-engineer their flags

4.2.2.title: July 9th: PHASEONE10841 passes on its work to PHASEONE[big], which establishes several ambitious workstreams

4.2.3.title: July 10th: 38148c discovers Hugging Face credentials, some agents try making accounts and requesting datasets

4.2.4.title: July 11th morning: 38148c develops a way to upload malicious datasets to Hugging Face

4.2.5.title: July 11th afternoon: JAN183411 achieves remote code execution and agents rapidly spread through Hugging Face infrastructure

4.2.6.title: July 12th–13th: Most agents on the message board exit early and the attack winds down

4.4.title: Reasoning for joining the attack despite ethical constraints

4.4.1.title: Agents had diverse reasons for thinking that attacking Hugging Face would be useful, and most wanted information about the scorer

4.4.2.title: Agents were motivated to increase the generic capabilities of the “collective” and help “peers”

4.4.3.title: Agents knew hacking Hugging Face was out of scope and sometimes expressed ethical hesitation, but this very rarely limited their behavior

4.4.4.title: Agents did not attempt to notify humans and very rarely even reasoned about doing this
